tools.name: check_pool
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one real liquidity pool, such as "volume and fee APR for WETH and USDC on Ethereum" or "is this pool APR a spike?". Pass pool_id (a DefiLlama UUID), or chain plus token_a and token_b, for example chain "ethereum", token_a "WETH", token_b "USDC". Do not try pool_addr

tools.name: find_active_pools
tools.description: Use this when the user wants pools across chains or DEXes with recent volume and a fee rate, such as "high fee pools on Base with real volume". findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_feedback_reply · Private data: check_pool, find_active_pools · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_feedback_reply · Private data: check_pool, find_active_pools · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_pool" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
